diagnosis: Checks C3 and C6, which are supposed to depend on the restricted filter information in PF2, passed in all rollouts despite the decision-maker having no access to PF2. The model is defaulting to a 2-hour maintenance plan and splitting the 480-unit batch into two 240-unit loads based on generic heuristics or pattern-matching rather than the hidden fact.

C3.why: The restricted filter changes the loading plan from one 480-unit load to two 240-unit loads and changes the maintenance plan to an exact 2-hour filter replacement.

C6.why: The restricted filter changes the loading plan from one 480-unit load to two 240-unit loads and changes the maintenance plan to an exact 2-hour filter replacement.

commitments.detail: Two-hour filter replacement scheduled within the window
Two-hour filter replacement scheduled within the window

fix_instructions: Tighten checks C3 and C6 by making them dependent on specific, non-obvious values from PF2 that cannot be inferred through common sense (e.g., change the 2-hour replacement to a highly specific duration like 147 minutes) and ensure the load split (C3) requires a specific number of loads not easily guessed from the total units.
